fpl.summary: The FPL analytics market splits into four tiers: (1) content giants (Fantasy Football Scout ~2.1M visits/mo, Fantasy Football Hub ~1.8M) that monetize daily editorial + licensed Opta/StatsBomb data but have shallow, opaque models; (2) tool/app products (Fantasy Football Fix ~970K visits, 230K Android downloads) selling black-box 'AI' projections at £4-8/mo; (3) free utility sites with enormous event-driven traffic (LiveFPL ~3.5M visits/mo — bigger than Scout — built on live rank + price predictions, free with ads, run by one academic); and (4) the quant niche (FPL Review ~24K visits, Patreon from ~$4.50/mo; FPL Optimized's open-source solver; AIrsenal; the 2025 OpenFPL paper which explicitly attacks FPL Review's paywalled irreproducibility). Key market events: FPL Statistics — once the default price-change site — is now DEFUNCT, and its traffic migrated to LiveFPL, proving free single-utility tools can capture millions of visits when an incumbent dies. Biggest exploitable gaps for evmax: (a) NOBODY combines rigorous probabilistic modeling with public methodology — FPL Review is the only serious model and it is paywalled/opaque (OpenFPL's academic critique validates evmax's transparency positioning); (b) nobody publishes distributions/ceilings/captain EV — everyone ships point-estimate xPts tables; (c) nobody offers a free JSON API, llms.txt, or any agent/LLM-citation optimization — the entire ecosystem is invisible-by-design to AI crawlers (JS-heavy dashboards, paywalls), so the LLM-answer channel is uncontested; (d) odds-based inputs are used naively (Fantasy Football Pundit just converts bookmaker odds to percentages, no de-vigging, no simulation) yet its free odds tables rank well in search — evmax's de-vigged Monte Carlo is a strict upgrade on a proven-demand content format; (e) accuracy accountability is absent — whatthef.pl exists solely to score other predictors, showing demand for verifiable track records that evmax can satisfy natively by publishing calibration. Pricing anchor for premium: £3.95-£10/mo (Fix £3.95-7.95, Scout £4.17-10, FPL Review ~$4.50+); free tier must be genuinely useful (LiveFPL/FPL Optimized set that expectation). Threat watch: Fix's ChatFPL and fpl.team/Hub 'AI' features show incumbents bolting LLMs onto their data, but none ground the LLM in transparent simulation output the way evmax does.

competitors.name: Fantasy Football Scout

competitors.weaknesses: No real predictive model of its own — 'model sophistication' is licensed data display plus a bolt-on 'AI Rating'; opinion-driven, not math-driven; key stats paywalled; site is ad-heavy and JS-heavy (poor agent/LLM accessibility); no API; methodology entirely opaque because there is no methodology to publish.

competitors.name: Fantasy Football Hub

competitors.pricing: Three tiers billed yearly — Starter (AI transfers, point predictions), Pro 'most popular' (expert/AI team reveals, 10+ pro tools, WhatsApp community), Ultra (monthly personal expert review, elite WhatsApp group, Zoom masterminds). Exact prices hidden behind trial flow; heavy perpetual discounting (currently '50% off for 2025/26'). Free trial on all tiers.

competitors.weaknesses: 'AI' is a marketing label — no published methodology, no accuracy track record; pricing deliberately obscured and discount-gimmicky; predictions locked behind paywall; upsell-heavy UX; no API, no agent accessibility; personality-dependent (expert reveals are the product more than the model).

competitors.content_cadence: High — daily articles in season, weekly expert team reveals, podcast, chip/blank-DGW guides.
competitors.traffic_signals: ~1.8M monthly visits (Similarweb Nov 2024); ~200K registered users; Android app on Google Play; active Discord + WhatsApp groups.

competitors.name: Fantasy Football Fix
competitors.what: The most productized FPL toolset: AI 'Assistant Manager' transfer recommendations, projected points, ChatFPL (LLM chatbot over Opta + projections), price-change predictor with push alerts, Elite XI live team reveals of top managers, future gameweek planner (5 draft teams), rotation planner, Opta sandbox, iOS/Android apps + Chrome extension.

competitors.name: FPL Review
competitors.what: The quant community's reference product: ML 'Massive Data Model' projections up to 14 GWs ahead (odds, team strength/style, player roles, penalties, rotation), premium Massive Data Planner, two solvers (MILP 'Linear Optimiser' + chess-engine-style Transfer Solver), Elite Data (top-1,000 manager ownership/captaincy), Season Review analytics, free planner with basic model.

competitors.strengths: Deepest genuine modeling in the market — the model top solvers and content creators cite; real optimization (MILP); docs site + video guides; Elite Data is unique; the de facto standard 'EV' source for the analytics community.
competitors.weaknesses: Tiny reach (~24.4K visits/mo, rank #125 in category — 1% of LiveFPL); paywalled model explicitly criticized in the 2025 OpenFPL arXiv paper for impeding reproducibility and independent benchmarking; dated UX; Patreon friction; no public API; projections are means, with limited distributional output; minimal content/SEO presence; effectively invisible to LLMs and casual managers.
competitors.model_sophistication: High — the benchmark. ML projections + true MILP solver + heuristic multi-week solver; methodology partially documented (docs.fplreview.com) but model itself closed and accuracy not independently auditable.
competitors.content_cadence: Low — occasional blog posts (e.g. 'Ultimate Truth' model-vs-perfect analysis); tool updates rather than content.
competitors.traffic_signals: ~24.4K monthly visits (Similarweb Nov 2025), #125 Fantasy Sports — small but extremely influential among elite/solver-community managers; Patreon subscriber base undisclosed.

competitors.name: LiveFPL
competitors.what: Free real-time utility suite by 'Ragabolly' (Mohamed Ragab, physics professor, ex-MIT/UChicago): live overall rank, live bonus/league tables, effective ownership by rank tier, tier expected-points averages, autosubs, transfer planner, and the now-default price-change predictor (98-99% claimed accuracy on rises).
competitors.pricing: Free with ads; ad-free access sold via Fantasy Football Scout's annual 'LiveFPL Bundle'; no standalone premium model of note.
competitors.strengths: Traffic monster: ~3.5M visits/mo (Nov 2025) — more than Scout; became the default price predictor after FPL Statistics died; deadline/matchday habit loop drives extreme repeat usage; free + fast + clear; trusted individual creator brand.
competitors.weaknesses: One-man project with no monetization ambition beyond ads/bundle; JS-rendered pages that fail for crawlers/agents (our fetch of the homepage returned nothing — invisible to LLMs); no projections/solver — descriptive not predictive; no API, no content, no SEO articles; keyperson risk; UX is utilitarian and ad-cluttered.
competitors.model_sophistication: Low-medium. Excellent live data engineering and a well-calibrated price-change heuristic; effective-ownership math; no player projection model, no optimization.
competitors.content_cadence: None (pure tool; updates in real time during matches).
competitors.traffic_signals: ~3.5M monthly visits (Similarweb Nov 2025), #18 Fantasy Sports category; distributed across livefpl.net, www2 and plan subdomains; large Twitter following.

competitors.name: FPL Statistics
competitors.what: Formerly the default price-change prediction site (the 'wildcard code' era institution). Both fplstatistics.co.uk and .com now refuse connections; third-party reviews (fplpredictionrater.co.uk, ThickAccent Nov 2025) describe it as defunct.
competitors.pricing: Was free with ads (historically had a small premium tier for extra columns).
competitors.strengths: None remaining — historical brand recognition only.
competitors.weaknesses: Dead. Its demise is the ecosystem's clearest lesson: a single-utility free tool owned massive habitual traffic, failed to modernize, and LiveFPL absorbed its entire audience within a season. Also spawned whatthef.pl, a meta-site that F1-scores the surviving predictors — evidence users want verifiable accuracy tracking.
competitors.model_sophistication: N/A (was a net-transfers heuristic model, opaque thresholds).
competitors.content_cadence: None (site down).
competitors.traffic_signals: Similarweb last profiled it June 2025; both domains unreachable July 2026 (ECONNREFUSED).

competitors.name: AIrsenal (Alan Turing Institute)

competitors.weaknesses: Not a product: no website, no UI, requires Python/WSL/Docker (PyPI install currently broken, issue #733); no chip optimization in transfer command; small reach (hundreds of technical users); no odds inputs — purely historical-data Bayesian model, weaker than odds-based approaches; no content or community for normal managers.

tourn.summary: Competitive audit of WC2026 tournament-fantasy + simulation content (July 2026, R32 done, R16 imminent). The field splits into four camps, and none of them combines what evmax does. (1) Fantasy-tips incumbents (Fantasy Football Scout ~2-3M visits/mo, Fantasy Football Hub) have the audience and SEO authority but their models are opaque, paywalled (£50/yr, annual-only), editorial-first, and have zero API/agent surface. (2) Prediction-model brands (Opta supercomputer 25k sims, Nate Silver's PELE 100k sims at $10/mo) have transparent-ish, credible simulation math and dominate media/LLM citations — but do NO fantasy layer at all: no xPts, no captain EV, no price-value. (3) Interactive simulator sites (WC2026Sim, Football Meets Data's simulator, ESPN's predictor, plus a long tail of ~10 thin clones) capture event-peak SEO with free Monte Carlo toys, but most use crude FIFA-rankings inputs, publish no analysis, and monetize weakly. (4) Social sim-graphics accounts — Football Meets Data is the biggest independent (126K X, 91K IG, built in ~2.5 years purely on daily probability graphics linking back to its simulator), plus We Global Football and TikTok bracket-sim creators; static probability tables/brackets and bubble-race animations are the winning formats, with link-in-bio → free tool as the standard funnel. The closest direct competitor is FantaLens (WC fantasy xPts for 1300+ players, Poisson+odds model, €9.99 one-time pass) — but it's tiny (~880 active managers), has no API, no articles, and no distribution. KEY GAPS FOR EVMAX: (a) nobody pairs credible de-vigged-odds simulation with fantasy xPts/captain EV AND transparent methodology — FantaLens is closest but subscale; (b) nobody offers a free JSON API or any agent/LLM optimization — Opta wins LLM citations today purely on domain authority, so evmax's llms.txt + per-article JSON is genuinely unique and attacks Opta's citation moat where it's structurally lazy; (c) proven growth channel is daily probability graphics on X/IG (FMD playbook) — evmax currently lacks this social distribution layer and should clone the format with fantasy-EV graphics (captain EV tables, xPts-per-price scatters) that no sim account posts; (d) the round-window cadence matters: Opta and FFS publish per-match previews daily during knockouts — evmax must match that tempo through R16→final, then pivot the same engine to FPL in August where Hub/Fix/Scout charge £30-70/yr for opaque xPts, leaving the same transparency+API gap open year-round.

competitors.name: Fantasy Football Scout (World Cup vertical)
competitors.what: The dominant UK fantasy-football content site, running a dedicated WC2026 vertical: ultimate guides per round (currently Round-of-32/knockouts), Scout Picks, 48-team previews, predicted lineups, mini-leagues with prizes, and a paid 'World Cup Fantasy Toolkit' (ownership widgets, fixture ticker, StatsBomb player/team data, xPts-based captaincy/differential/bargain widgets, AI Team Ratings, draft/AI-rating tool).
competitors.pricing: Chief Scout membership £50/yr or £10/mo ('lowest 2026 prices'); monthly option marketed specifically for WC-only subscribers; core articles free and ad-supported.
competitors.strengths: Massive brand and community; #2 UK fantasy-sports site with huge SEO domain authority; StatsBomb data partnership; full editorial machine (multiple posts/day, big-name manager team reveals); established monetization ladder already tuned for event traffic.
competitors.weaknesses: Methodology completely opaque — xPts are a black-box widget behind the paywall; editorial-first, numbers-second; no public API, no JSON, no llms.txt or agent optimization; toolkit is widgets not simulations (no Monte Carlo, no captain EV distributions/ceilings); WC vertical is a sideline to FPL, so knockout-specific modeling (extra time, pens, advancement-conditional minutes) is thin.
competitors.traffic_signals: Similarweb: ~2.1M visits/mo (Nov 2024 datapoint), 3.2M in Sep 2024 peaks; ranked #2 UK fantasy-sports website (Apr 2026); global rank ~30k; 78% male, 25-34 core.
competitors.content_cadence: Multiple articles daily during the World Cup; per-round mega-guides, Scout Picks per round, team news and lineup posts around every matchday.
competitors.model_sophistication: Low-medium: StatsBomb event data and proprietary xPts projections, but no visible simulation layer, no de-vigged market inputs disclosed, no uncertainty/ceiling outputs; 'AI Team Ratings' marketed without methodology.

competitors.name: Fantasy Football Hub
competitors.what: FPL-first tips site with ML positioning ('Hub AI' predicted points, team rating, transfer suggestions) running a WC2026 side-vertical: Ultimate Round-of-32 guide, £500 WC Fantasy prize league, app-based tools.
competitors.pricing: Three membership tiers, all billed annually (roughly £30-70/yr range historically); 7-day free trial; frequent 30% discount codes; WC prize league free to enter as acquisition funnel.
competitors.strengths: Strongest 'AI' branding in the fantasy-tips space; polished iOS/Android app; expert roster (top-1k FPL managers); prize leagues drive email capture; established paying subscriber base to cross-sell WC content to.
competitors.weaknesses: WC coverage is clearly a bolt-on to FPL — far thinner than Scout's; Hub AI is fully opaque (no methodology page, no probabilities, no simulations); annual-only billing is a poor fit for a 5-week tournament; no API, no agent/LLM surface; predicted points shown without uncertainty.

competitors.name: FantaLens
competitors.what: Closest direct competitor: independent, fan-made WC2026 fantasy analytics tool — live xPts projections for 1300+ players, AI Squad Coach (one-tap squad rebuild, captain/booster planning, differential hunting with the low-ownership scouting bonus modeled), Player Explorer, fixture difficulty from Poisson model blended with live betting odds, start-probability/rotation model.

competitors.weaknesses: Tiny — claims only ~880 active managers; no content/SEO layer (no articles, so no search or citation surface); no public API or data export; anonymous team, no brand trust; no social distribution; methodology described only at a high level (no de-vig detail, no sim counts, no ceilings/variance); dies after the final unless it pivots.
competitors.traffic_signals: ~880 active managers self-reported; negligible search presence beyond its own name; live Telegram chat.
competitors.content_cadence: Data refreshed daily during the tournament (stats, lineups, FIFA prices, market odds); no editorial cadence.

competitors.name: Opta Analyst (Opta supercomputer / The Analyst)
competitors.what: Stats Perform's free content arm. WC2026 coverage: supercomputer tournament forecasts from 25,000 simulations, a live knockout bracket page whose percentages 'update with every goal and full-time result', plus an individual data-driven match preview article for every WC fixture (win probs, key stats).

competitors.weaknesses: Zero fantasy layer (no xPts, captain, price-value — irrelevant to fantasy managers directly); methodology only loosely described (team ratings + betting-market flavored, but no de-vig transparency, no downloadable probabilities); no API, no JSON, no llms.txt — its citation moat is pure domain authority, structurally lazy and attackable by machine-readable alternatives; corporate tone, no community or email product; no interactivity beyond the bracket page.
competitors.traffic_signals: Syndicated into major outlets (Al Jazeera daily WC schedule/prediction posts embed its numbers); theanalyst.com rides tournament peaks hard; exact visits not public but clearly the highest-reach model brand in this audit.
competitors.content_cadence: Daily during the WC: one preview article per match plus bracket/forecast refresh after every result; weekly supercomputer roundups.
competitors.model_sophistication: High: 25k tournament simulations over market-informed team ratings, stage-conditional probabilities, live in-tournament updating — but presented as authority ('the supercomputer says') rather than transparent math.

competitors.name: WC2026Sim (SimuMatch network)
competitors.what: Pure-SEO interactive simulator: full 48-team/12-group/R32 official-format tournament sim, 10,000 Monte Carlo runs off FIFA rankings (April 2026 baseline), editable team strengths, forced-result scenarios, shareable outputs, friend prediction pools, bubble-animation visual mode, plus programmatic pages (FIFA-ranking page etc.).
competitors.pricing: Free, no signup; no visible subscription; presumably display-ad/affiliate monetization; part of the broader SimuMatch sports-sim platform.
competitors.strengths: Ranks on high-intent 'world cup 2026 simulator' queries; instant-gratification interactivity and shareable scenarios; prediction pools add light retention; format-accurate (best-3rd-place logic).
competitors.weaknesses: Crude model — FIFA rankings with an April baseline, no odds, no Elo blend, unclear in-tournament updating; zero analysis/editorial so no citation value; anonymous operator, no brand; no fantasy content whatsoever; no API/data; traffic evaporates after July 19.
competitors.traffic_signals: Multiple top-10 organic slots for simulator queries (main page, /simulate, /ranking all indexed); no audience metrics public; one of ~10 near-identical long-tail sim sites (sim2026.com, wc26.org, cupsimulator.com, worldcup2026-simulator.com, fifaschedule.com, ESPN's own free predictor + bracket challenge).
competitors.content_cadence: Static tool; rankings baseline updated seasonally (April 2026); no editorial output.
competitors.model_sophistication: Low: 10k Monte Carlo runs but inputs are FIFA rankings only — a toy next to odds- or Elo-based engines.

competitors.name: Football Meets Data
competitors.what: Independent analytics brand spanning a free simulator platform (WC2026 + all 54 European top divisions: 10k/20k/50k Monte Carlo runs on Elo blended with de facto live betting-market implied probabilities, covering ET and penalties, force-a-result scenario testing) and the biggest independent social sim-graphics operation (daily probability tables, qualification scenarios, 'X% to win the trophy' graphics).
competitors.pricing: Simulator free; no visible premium tier or API pricing; monetization appears to be audience-building first (site traffic + possible future premium), making it a land-grab competitor rather than a revenue machine.
competitors.strengths: Best methodology communication in the free tier — publishes blog posts explaining the Elo+market blend and why; social flywheel proven (grew X account from zero in Oct 2023 to 126K by 2026 purely on probability graphics); scenario interactivity; covers the exact 'transparent math' lane evmax claims, at the match/tournament level.
competitors.weaknesses: No fantasy layer at all — no xPts, prices, captaincy, EV-per-price; no public API or data downloads; site is thin relative to the social presence (the product is really the X account); no email/premium ladder visible; probabilities without written analysis articles at depth, so weak on long-form SEO and LLM citation vs Opta.
competitors.traffic_signals: X @fmeetsdata 126.1K followers (account created Oct 2023 — fastest riser in the niche); Instagram @football.meets.data 91K followers / 6,800+ posts; Facebook + Threads presence; simulator page ranks top-5 for WC-simulator queries.
competitors.content_cadence: Multiple graphics/posts daily on X/IG; simulator probabilities refreshed as results come in; occasional methodology blog posts.
competitors.model_sophistication: Medium-high: Elo + live-betting-market blend feeding 10k-50k Monte Carlo tournament sims including ET/penalties — closest public analogue to evmax's de-vigged-odds engine, minus the fantasy translation.

competitors.name: We Global Football
competitors.what: Long-running international-football analytics/journalism site: Monte Carlo-style qualification and tournament probabilities across all confederations (WC qualifiers, Nations League, AFCON 2027), rankings, watch-lists, plus purchasable tournament trackers (spreadsheet products), a merch store and consulting services; distribution via X @We_Global probability graphics.
competitors.pricing: Site content free; sells one-off tournament trackers and merch; offers consulting; no subscription found.
competitors.strengths: Rare full-confederation coverage (deep on CONCACAF/CAF/AFC qualifiers where nobody else models); years of continuity and a niche-respected brand among international-football nerds; tracker products prove willingness-to-pay for structured data files.
competitors.weaknesses: Almost invisible in WC2026 search results this cycle — outcompeted by Opta/FMD/simulator sites; methodology undisclosed on site; dated web presence, no interactive tools; small social footprint (@We_Global follower count not even surfaced in search); no fantasy content, no API; publishing gaps suggest limited resources.
competitors.traffic_signals: Weak: did not appear organically in any WC2026-prediction search in this audit; X account active but modest; homepage article dates show irregular output.
competitors.content_cadence: Irregular; qualifier-window driven historically; not matching daily knockout tempo this tournament.
competitors.model_sophistication: Medium historically (Monte Carlo qualification probabilities) but unverifiable this cycle — methodology not published.

competitors.name: Silver Bulletin — PELE model (Nate Silver)
competitors.what: The FiveThirtyEight successor for this niche: Nate Silver's new PELE model ('Predictive Elo with Lineup Equilibria' — Elo variant incorporating player market values/ages, match results, economic/geographic priors) running 100,000 tournament simulations, updated after every WC match with knockout-stage prediction posts; full ratings suite for paid subscribers; notes/commentary comparing PELE to betting markets (e.g., docking France to 11.7% vs market 17% pre-tournament).
competitors.pricing: Substack: $10/mo or $95/yr (grandfathered $8/$80 pre-June-2025); headline WC posts partially free, full PELE ratings paywalled.
competitors.strengths: Strongest personal brand in prediction media; genuinely transparent methodology posts (dedicated PELE-methodology article); 100k sims with performance-updating priors; large existing newsletter audience to funnel; media pickup (RealClearMarkets etc.); explicitly frames edges vs the betting market — closest philosophical neighbor to evmax's de-vig framing.
competitors.weaknesses: No fantasy application at all; no interactive tools, no API, no data downloads (a step back from 538's famous CSV repos); international-only so far (club/FPL extension only 'under consideration'); newsletter cadence not per-match; paywall blocks LLM/citation flow of the full numbers; one-man-brand risk and US-politics-first audience.
competitors.traffic_signals: Silver Bulletin is one of Substack's largest paid publications (hundreds of thousands of free subscribers, tens of thousands paid — exact figures unpublished); WC posts circulate widely on X/Substack Notes.
competitors.content_cadence: Model updates after every match; written knockout-round prediction posts roughly weekly-to-biweekly plus live notes.
competitors.model_sophistication: High: 100k Monte Carlo tournament sims, Elo + player-market-value hybrid, tiebreaker-exact group modeling, in-tournament form updating, explicit market-vs-model comparisons — but closed data.

competitors.name: Social simulation-graphics ecosystem (X/IG/TikTok bracket-odds accounts)
competitors.what: The distribution layer for simulation content. Biggest independent: Football Meets Data (X 126K, IG 91K) posting daily probability tables, 'chance to win the trophy' bars, and scenario graphics linking to its simulator. Second tier: We Global Football (@We_Global) qualification-probability graphics; xG-adjacent giants like @xGPhilosophy (xG scorelines, ~600K-class reach) that occasionally amplify tournament odds; corporate accounts (OptaJoe/OptaAnalyst, millions of followers) pushing supercomputer graphics; EA SPORTS' official 'FC predicts the World Cup' PR sim (mass-media pickup). TikTok is dominated not by stats accounts but by bracket-predictor gameplay videos, eFootball/FC26 'simulated the final' clips and AI-edit trends under #worldcup2026 (billions of views); TikTok is FIFA's official video partner for 2026.
competitors.pricing: Free content; monetization via link-in-bio to tools/sites, occasional sponsored posts and affiliate links; We Global sells tracker files; no paywalls on the graphics themselves.
competitors.strengths: Proven, fast audience compounding (FMD: 0→126K in ~2.5 years off pure probability graphics); static tables/brackets and bubble/marble-race animations are endlessly repeatable formats; graphics get screenshot-syndicated into group chats and media, building brand beyond follower counts.
competitors.weaknesses: Nobody in the sim-graphics niche posts FANTASY-EV graphics (captain EV tables, xPts-per-price scatters, ceiling distributions) — the format is unclaimed; most accounts have no product behind the link (or a free toy), so conversion ladders are weak; TikTok sim content is entertainment (game-engine sims), leaving the data-sim lane nearly empty there; graphics are un-cited/un-linkable by LLMs (images, no structured data).
competitors.traffic_signals: FMD: 126.1K X / 91K IG / 6.8K+ IG posts. OptaJoe: multi-million (corporate). #worldcup2026 TikTok: billions of views, >10B total WC social posts projected. Independent data-sim accounts on TikTok: effectively absent (gap).
competitors.content_cadence: Daily to multiple-times-daily during the tournament; graphics within minutes-to-hours of full-time results perform best.
competitors.model_sophistication: Varies: FMD medium-high (its own Elo+market engine), We Global medium, most TikTok 'sims' zero (video-game simulations); presentation sophistication matters more than model depth for reach.

betting.summary: The betting-stats/odds-content landscape splits into three clusters, and none occupies evmax's position of free + transparent + machine-readable. (1) PRO EV TOOLS (OddsJam, Unabated): methodologically honest — they openly de-vig sharp lines, exactly evmax's core math — but they are $99–$999/mo paywalled software, US-sport-centric, prop/arb-scanner shaped, produce no narrative content, no soccer/fantasy depth, and are invisible to LLM citation because their value lives behind login. (2) US BETTING MEDIA (Action Network, Covers, Pickswise, Dimers, SBR): high traffic (1.9M–6M visits/mo) monetized via sportsbook affiliate CPA plus subscriptions, but every model is a black box — 'proprietary power ratings', 'AI-powered simulations', 'expert blends' — with no published methodology, no de-vig details, no calibration/Brier scores, no public backtests, and clear affiliate conflicts of interest. Soccer/World Cup is an afterthought for all of them. (3) SOCCER PREDICTION/STATS SITES (Forebet 10–18M visits/mo, WinDrawWin, SofaScore 105M visits/mo, FootyStats): enormous organic traffic proving demand for quantitative soccer predictions, but universally opaque algorithms (Forebet admits Poisson but publishes no weights, backtests or calibration; independent audits peg it at ~62% 1X2 vs marketed 75%+), ad-cluttered 2005-era UX, zero fantasy-points layer, no APIs for content, and no agent/LLM optimization whatsoever. THE GAP EVMAX CAN OWN: (a) transparency itself — literally no content site publishes de-vig method, sim counts, calibration curves or honest error tracking; evmax's 'show the math' stance is unoccupied; (b) the odds→fantasy-xPts translation — EV tools stop at bet EV, prediction sites stop at 1X2/correct-score, nobody converts market odds into player xPts/captain EV/ceilings; (c) machine-readability — no competitor has llms.txt, per-article JSON, or an AI-crawler strategy, so LLM answers about 'best World Cup captain picks' have no quantitative source to cite; (d) free tier of what OddsJam charges $199/mo for, monetized later via the email→premium→API ladder; (e) event-peak soccer — US sites under-serve World Cup/FPL, soccer sites under-serve EV thinking. Biggest threats: Dimers (closest analogue: sims + free content + cheap Pro at $29.99/mo, but US-focused and still opaque) and Forebet's entrenched SEO for soccer-prediction queries. Attack vector: out-transparent everyone, publish calibration receipts, and be the citable source when agents answer betting/fantasy questions during the Round of 16 and the August FPL launch.

competitors.name: Oddschecker (editorial)
competitors.what: UK's #1 odds-comparison grid plus editorial layer: daily tips, horse-racing naps, football accas, free-bet/offer pages, 'Oddschecker Endorsed' operator promos. Owned by FairPlay Sports Media.
competitors.pricing: Free to users; monetized via bookmaker affiliate/CPA, CPM display ads, and operator brand deals (~$70M annual revenue reported).
competitors.content_cadence: Daily, high volume — tips for every major race/match day, offer pages refreshed constantly.
competitors.model_sophistication: None. Editorial tips are human tipster opinion; the odds grid is raw prices with no de-vig, no probabilities, no EV. Insight = 'odds movement' at best.
competitors.traffic_signals: ~5.7–7.4M visits/month (Similarweb/Semrush, spring 2026); 55M+ annual UK sessions; very strong direct + brand SEO.
competitors.strengths: Massive brand trust in UK, real-time price coverage of 100M+ live prices, huge distribution, deep bookmaker relationships, soccer-native audience.
competitors.weaknesses: Zero model transparency because there is zero model — tips are vibes with affiliate links; conflicted incentives (paid 'Endorsed' operators); no probabilities, no fantasy layer, no API, no LLM optimization. A reader who wants 'why is this a good bet, numerically' gets nothing.

competitors.name: OddsJam
competitors.what: Positive-EV/arbitrage/middles scanner across 100+ US sportsbooks: real-time odds screen, +EV bet feed, promo converters, bet tracker. Tool, not content site.
competitors.pricing: Tiered subs ~$39–49/mo entry (odds screen) up to $199/mo standard +EV and ~$500–999/mo Platinum/Global; 7-day free trial; annual saves 20–30%.
competitors.content_cadence: Continuous tool data; thin SEO blog/education layer, minimal narrative analysis.
competitors.model_sophistication: High and honest about mechanism: de-vigs sharp reference books to compute fair value and flags +EV lines — the same math evmax uses. But it outputs bet lists, not analysis.
competitors.traffic_signals: Niche pro/semi-pro audience; growth via YouTube/affiliate reviewers; acquired traffic far smaller than media sites but high-LTV subscribers.
competitors.strengths: Genuinely quantitative, real-time, per-book coverage; trusted by serious bettors; proven willingness-to-pay validates the 'EV from de-vigged odds' product at $199+/mo.
competitors.weaknesses: Expensive paywall excludes casual bettors; US-sport and promo-farming centric, weak soccer and zero fantasy; no explanatory content — it tells you WHAT is +EV, never WHY; nothing public for LLMs to cite; books limit winners, capping the addressable market.

competitors.name: Unabated
competitors.what: Sharp-bettor toolkit by Rufus Peabody/Jack Andrews: 'Unabated Line' (vig-free consensus of market-making books), props simulator, calculators, alt-line pricing, betting education podcast/articles.
competitors.pricing: Props+ $99/mo; Premium $199/mo; NBA projections add-on $249/mo. Some free calculators and education content.
competitors.content_cadence: Tool is real-time; editorial/education is occasional (articles, podcast), not daily picks.
competitors.model_sophistication: Highest in the space — explicitly explains de-vigging, market-making book weighting, and simulation logic; respected as 'the gold standard' for fair lines.
competitors.traffic_signals: Small but elite audience of sharps; influence far exceeds traffic; commonly cited in betting-Twitter discourse.
competitors.strengths: Credibility and methodological transparency at the tool level; education content is best-in-class; proof that 'de-vigged fair line' is a sellable primitive.
competitors.weaknesses: $199/mo gate, US-major-sport focus (NFL/NBA/MLB props), effectively no soccer and no fantasy-points translation; produces almost no indexable analysis per event, so it wins zero SEO/LLM-citation traffic; intimidating to non-sharps.

competitors.name: Pickswise
competitors.what: Free expert picks, props, parlays and same-game parlays across US sports plus soccer; app-first; 'expert analyst' write-ups per game.
competitors.pricing: 100% free to users; pure sportsbook affiliate model (FanDuel etc. sign-up CPA).
competitors.content_cadence: Very high — daily picks across every major sport/slate, templated match previews.
competitors.model_sophistication: None disclosed. Human handicapper narrative ('form, dynamics, factors'); no probabilities, no EV, no track-record ledger; Reddit users report best-bets hitting ~25% in bad stretches with no accountability.
competitors.traffic_signals: ~1.9M visits/month (Semrush, late 2025), declining month-over-month in tracked periods; strong app presence.
competitors.strengths: Free removes friction; huge content volume ranks for '[game] prediction' queries; clean modern UX; parlay/SGP content matches casual demand.
competitors.weaknesses: Textbook opaque-picks site: zero math shown, zero verified records, affiliate conflict baked into every page. This is exactly the credibility vacuum a transparent-methodology site attacks; its soccer previews are shallow and stat-light.

competitors.name: Covers.com
competitors.what: Legacy (since 1995) betting media hub: odds, matchup pages, free + paid expert picks, public-consensus data, contests (Streak Survivor, King of Covers), forum, sportsbook reviews.
competitors.pricing: Free core; premium handicapper picks $10–$99; affiliate CPA on sportsbook reviews/Sportsbook Matcher; ads.
competitors.content_cadence: Daily across all US sports + World Cup odds pages; contests refresh daily.
competitors.model_sophistication: Low. Consensus = crowd pick percentages, not probabilities; paid picks are unaudited human handicappers; no de-vig, no simulations, no published methodology.
competitors.traffic_signals: ~6M visits/month, growing ~14% MoM recently, global rank ~8,650 (Similarweb); 58% direct traffic = strong loyal community.
competitors.strengths: 25-year brand, sticky community/contests, consensus data is a unique (if crude) dataset, ranks well for odds queries including World Cup.
competitors.weaknesses: Selling $10–99 unverified handicapper picks is the anti-transparency model; consensus percentages get misread as edges; dated UX; soccer coverage is odds-listing, not analysis; no API, no agent-readiness.

competitors.name: Action Network
competitors.what: Premium US betting media: news, expert picks, PRO Report (sharp-money signals, betting systems), projections pages per sport, bet tracking app. Owned by Better Collective ($240M, 2021).
competitors.pricing: PRO ~$19.99/week with heavily discounted annual; Action Labs $249/mo or ~$125/mo annual; plus affiliate revenue. Revenue ~$35M/yr.
competitors.content_cadence: High — daily articles, projections updated per slate, podcasts, breaking news.
competitors.model_sophistication: Medium but opaque: 'proprietary power ratings' and 'projection blends of key experts' with letter-graded edges. Method, inputs and weights undisclosed; no calibration or public backtests; sharp-action signals unverifiable.
competitors.traffic_signals: ~3.2M visits/month, US rank ~4,400 (Similarweb Feb 2026); 52% bounce; strong brand among US bettors.
competitors.strengths: Best-funded editorial in the space, real data assets (public betting %, sharp signals), strong app and bet-sync retention loop, credible expert brands.
competitors.weaknesses: 'Trust our proprietary blend' is the exact opposite of showing the math; expert-blend projections are subjective; expensive; almost entirely US sports — World Cup/FPL coverage thin; affiliate owner (Better Collective) deepens conflict; no public API/JSON, no LLM optimization.

competitors.name: Dimers
competitors.what: Closest analogue to evmax: AI/simulation-driven predictions site (Cipher Sports) — 10,000+ sims per game, win probabilities, best bets, props, parlays, Dimebot conversational assistant, free tier + Pro.
competitors.pricing: Freemium: core predictions free (affiliate-monetized); Dimers Pro $14.99/wk, $29.99/mo, $199.99/yr; 3-day trial.
competitors.content_cadence: Very high — every US slate simulated daily, templated pick articles per game, news posts.
competitors.model_sophistication: Medium-high mechanics, low transparency: claims 10k simulations, 100k+ data points/sport, 15 yrs modeling — but publishes no methodology doc, no de-vig detail, no calibration curves or verified ROI ledger. 'AI-powered' is marketing surface.
competitors.traffic_signals: US rank ~15,000, global ~64,000 (Similarweb); roughly ~1M visits/mo scale; claims '10M+ fans'; pages/visit 3.6.
competitors.strengths: Proves the exact evmax content shape works commercially (sims → probabilities → free articles → cheap sub); Dimebot shows appetite for conversational/agent access to model output; strong pick-page SEO templates.
competitors.weaknesses: Simulations are a black box — no method page, no error tracking, no downloadable data; US-centric (NFL/NBA/MLB/CBB), soccer and World Cup are shallow add-ons, no fantasy-points layer at all; affiliate links throughout free tier; no llms.txt/JSON API — its model output is not agent-citable.

competitors.name: Sportsbook Review (SBR)
competitors.what: 1999-era industry watchdog turned betting media: sportsbook ratings/reviews, odds board, free picks across sports, large legacy forum, community contests.
competitors.pricing: Free; monetized via sportsbook affiliate placements and ads (now US-books-focused after change of ownership).
competitors.content_cadence: Daily picks/news; forum continuous but aging.
competitors.model_sophistication: None. Picks are staff write-ups; odds board is raw lines; no modeling claims at all.
competitors.traffic_signals: Diminished from its 2000s peak; community complains of censorship and decline post-acquisition; still ranks for sportsbook-review queries.
competitors.strengths: Deep trust legacy as a watchdog, long-running forum knowledge base, strong review-query SEO.
competitors.weaknesses: Strategically adrift — neither a real tool nor a real model; watchdog credibility eroded by affiliate ownership; zero quantitative content; effectively no threat on analysis, only on 'best sportsbook' queries.

competitors.name: Forebet
competitors.what: The dominant mathematical football-prediction site: Poisson-based 1X2/correct-score/O-U probabilities, 'Value' section (Kelly vs bookie odds), standings/trends for hundreds of leagues worldwide, World Cup pages.
competitors.pricing: Free, ad-supported (heavy display ads); no premium tier of note.
competitors.content_cadence: Automated daily — every fixture in hundreds of leagues gets a probability row; no real editorial.
competitors.model_sophistication: Medium mechanics, poor transparency: admits Poisson + Kelly-vs-odds framing but publishes no variable weights, no backtests, no Brier/calibration; marketing claims 75%+ accuracy while independent 2025 audits measured ~62% 1X2. Odds used as calibration input (so partly circular).
competitors.traffic_signals: Huge: ~10.1M visits/mo (Semrush April 2026) to ~18.2M (Similarweb), 12+ min sessions; top competitor Predictz ~3.5M, WinDrawWin ~2.2M. Global-south heavy audience.
competitors.strengths: Owns global SEO for 'football predictions today'; total-fixture coverage; probability-per-match format users clearly want; long-session engagement.
competitors.weaknesses: The most attackable incumbent: black-box model with accuracy claims contradicted by audits, brutal ad-cluttered UX, no de-vigging discipline, no fantasy layer, no API/llms.txt, no articles explaining reasoning, English-language editorial nearly nonexistent. A transparent, calibrated, well-designed alternative with published error tracking directly undercuts its credibility.

competitors.name: WinDrawWin
competitors.what: Free football tips/predictions since 2003: 1X2 predictions with stake-size labels, acca tips, BTTS/over-under/corners/HT stats tables across dozens of leagues.
competitors.pricing: Free; ad + bookmaker affiliate monetized ('free bet offers'); sells ad slots directly.
competitors.content_cadence: Automated daily prediction tables for all covered leagues.
competitors.model_sophistication: Low: vague 'historical data + form + trends' methodology, never documented; outputs picks and scorelines, not probabilities; no accuracy ledger.
competitors.traffic_signals: ~1.2–2.2M visits/month (Semrush/Similarweb), ~8 min sessions; solid legacy SEO.
competitors.strengths: 20+ year domain authority, useful raw stat tables (BTTS/corners) that rank well, simple format casual punters like.
competitors.weaknesses: No probabilities at all (just W/D/W calls), no methodology, dated design, no EV concept, no fantasy angle, no machine-readable output. Vulnerable to any site pairing its stat-table SEO shape with real math.

competitors.name: SofaScore (predictions/betting layer)
competitors.what: Massive live-score/stats platform (2000+ leagues, player ratings, heatmaps) with a betting layer: 'Who will win?' crowd votes, dropping-odds pages, betting-tips section, bookmaker integrations.
competitors.pricing: Free; monetized via advertising (bookmaker-heavy) and B2B data/media partnerships; app IAP for ad removal.
competitors.content_cadence: Real-time, fully automated; no editorial analysis.
competitors.model_sophistication: Low for predictions: crowd-vote percentages and raw odds, explicitly no AI/model predictions (cited as a 2026 weakness vs newer apps); its xG/player-rating data is sophisticated but not turned into forecasts.
competitors.traffic_signals: Enormous: ~104.7M visits/month, 15+ min sessions (Semrush May 2026); global audience led by Brazil/Nigeria/Indonesia.
competitors.strengths: Unmatched reach and data depth, real-time xG and ratings, the default second-screen app worldwide — any 'stats for this match' query funnels here.
competitors.weaknesses: Deliberately stops short of analysis: no probabilities from its own data, no EV, no written reasoning, no fantasy xPts; crowd votes are noise. Its scale is a distribution moat, not an analysis moat — it leaves the 'so what should I do with these stats' layer completely open.

competitors.name: FootyStats
competitors.what: Betting-oriented football stats database: O/U, BTTS%, corners, cards, form and H2H splits for 1,500+ competitions; per-league/team/player pages; data API.
competitors.pricing: Freemium: free tier limited; Premium ~£10–15/mo (top-30 leagues); Pro ~£20–25/mo (150+ leagues, history, API access).
competitors.content_cadence: Automated stat updates; minimal editorial; some templated prediction pages.
competitors.model_sophistication: Low-medium: rich descriptive stats but predictions are trend extrapolation, not modeled probabilities; users flag prediction accuracy and odds misalignment; no de-vig or EV framework.
competitors.traffic_signals: ~3.4M visits/month, 12+ min sessions, +14% MoM (Semrush March 2026).
competitors.strengths: Best breadth of betting-relevant soccer stats (corners/cards/BTTS) at low price; existing paid API proves demand for machine-readable soccer data; strong niche-league coverage.
competitors.weaknesses: Descriptive, not predictive — stats without a model, EV, or simulation; trend stats invite base-rate errors; no narrative analysis, no calibration, no fantasy layer; API is data-out only, not analysis. Complements rather than substitutes for what evmax does — and shows an API monetization path.

agentSurface.summary: Agent-surface audit of 11 competitor domains (fetched 2026-07-03): only ONE domain (theanalyst.com) actively blocks AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai, CCBot, Google-Extended all Disallow: /), and only ONE domain (dimers.com) has an llms.txt — a full LLM-oriented site guide, making it the single competitor deliberately courting agent traffic. footystats.org goes the other way on crawling (explicit Crawl-delay rules that WELCOME ClaudeBot at delay 1 and PerplexityBot at delay 10) and is the only one with a public, documented (paid) JSON API — but it firewalls its /api/* paths from crawlers. Everything else (fplreview, fantasyfootballscout, fantasyfootballhub, fantasyfootballfix, livefpl, oddschecker, actionnetwork, forebet) has generic or absent robots.txt, no llms.txt, and no public API — their numbers live behind Patreon/premium paywalls or unstructured HTML, i.e. invisible or unusable to agents. Net: the fantasy-football vertical's agent surface is essentially unclaimed; evmax's llms.txt + free per-article JSON + AI-crawler allow-list has no direct FPL/fantasy competitor, and its only llms.txt rival (dimers) is a US-betting affiliate site, not a fantasy-EV site. The premium data brand (Opta/theanalyst) actively opting OUT of LLM ingestion means agents seeking "the stats behind the pick" cannot cite the biggest authority — a citation vacuum evmax can fill during the World Cup window.

findings.detail: robots.txt: WordPress default (User-agent: *, Disallow: /wp-admin/ only) — no AI-bot rules, so GPTBot/ClaudeBot/PerplexityBot/Google-Extended are allowed by default but not courted. No llms.txt (404). No public API: projections (Massive Data Planner) are Patreon-gated; docs.fplreview.com documents the models/tools but no data endpoints. Structured data: standard WP sitemap only. Verdict: the strongest FPL-projection competitor is completely dark to agents — its xPts numbers are paywalled and uncitable.
findings.evidence: https://fplreview.com/robots.txt ; https://fplreview.com/llms.txt (404) ; https://docs.fplreview.com/ ; fplreview.com/access-the-massive-data-planner (Patreon required)

findings.detail: robots.txt: fully permissive (User-agent: *, empty Disallow), no AI-bot rules, sitemap_index.xml present. No llms.txt (404). No API; core content (Season Ticket, projections) is membership-paywalled. Verdict: allows AI crawling passively but offers agents nothing structured — articles only, numbers behind login.

Retrieval is dominated by four fantasy-content incumbents (allaboutfpl.com, rotowire.com, fantasyfootballscout.co.uk, fantasyfootballhub.co.uk), the official premierleague.com (total monopoly on captain queries), and big media (yahoo/fox/espn) on predictions/betting queries. However, evmax's exact core competency — simulation/xPts/Monte-Carlo queries — has the WEAKEST incumbents: hobby one-page simulators, substacks, GitHub repos, arxiv papers and even PBN spam occupy top slots, and young low-authority sites (fplcopilot.com, thefantasytool.com, fantalens.com) already rank #1 there, proving these queries are winnable without domain authority. Biggest gaps to attack now: "world cup fantasy expected points simulation", "world cup 2026 simulation odds", "monte carlo simulation fantasy football", "fpl expected points model", "football match predictions statistical model". Hardest to win: captain-pick and best-team queries (premierleague.com / rotowire / allaboutfpl entrenched) and match-prediction/betting queries (big media + sportsbooks).
